The Godfather (1972).sign: The Bronx, New York. The best veal in the city.

note.text: Order the veal, it's the best in the city. Then leave the gun, take the cannoli.

The Godfather Part II (1974).sign: Vedado, Havana. New Year's Eve, 1958. Champagne at midnight.

note.text: One glass at midnight, then we go home. Fredo, stay where I can see you.
Anthony sings tonight, so nobody leaves before the last act. The cannoli can wait for the curtain call.

Goodfellas (1990).sign: Lewisburg, Pennsylvania. Dinner, cell block wing.

note.text: Paulie's on garlic, Vinnie's on sauce, and I've got the steaks. Prison dinner never looked this good.

A Bronx Tale (1993).sign: Belmont Avenue, the Bronx. 1960. Members only.

note.text: Sit with your back to the wall and finish the rigatoni. A clean plate tells me more about a man than his car does.

Once Upon a Time in America (1984).sign: Delancey Street, Lower East Side. 1933. Knock twice.

note.text: Back room's set for the four of you, same as always. The brisket's been going since breakfast, so nobody's allowed to be late.

Carlito's Way (1993).sign: Spanish Harlem, New York. 1975. Dancing till late.

note.text: Pernil's on, the band's warming up, and Gail's packed for the islands. One more good night and I'm done.

Donnie Brasco (1997).sign: New York. 1978. Shoes off in the tatami room.

note.text: Take your shoes off before you sit, I'm not telling you twice. Then eat, because the steak won't keep while you argue.

Mean Streets (1973).sign: Little Italy, New York. San Gennaro week. Jukebox on.

note.text: Johnny Boy owes half the room money, so tonight he's buying the calamari. I'll keep his plate warm just in case.

Casino (1995).sign: Tangiers Hotel and Casino, Las Vegas. 1973. Open all night.

note.text: Every plate goes out looking exactly the same, and I'll be checking. The guests get what the high rollers get.

Scarface (1983).sign: Miami Beach. 1980. Booths by the stage.

note.text: Order whatever you like, the table's on me. Save some pastelitos for Manny, he's out on the dance floor again.

The Untouchables (1987).sign: Michigan Avenue, Chicago. 1930. Banquet room, cold tea by the cup.

note.text: A man stands alone at the plate. At this table we eat as a team, and nobody touches the beef till every plate is down.

Prizzi's Honor (1985).sign: Court Street, Brooklyn. Nobody leaves before the cake.

note.text: The ziti's for family, the almond cookies are for everyone. Charley, stop staring at the lady in lavender and pass the bread.

Analyze This (1999).sign: Grand Ballroom, New York. A private dinner of the families.

note.text: The doc says I should share my feelings, so here goes. I feel like the veal parm is the best thing that happened to me this week.

Mickey Blue Eyes (1999).sign: Little Italy, New York. Family tables only.

note.text: Michael, you're family now, so the linguine's free. Just don't try that Kansas City accent near the kitchen again.

The Pope of Greenwich Village (1984).sign: Bleecker Street, Greenwich Village. Dinner from five, staff meal after.

note.text: Waiters eat after the last table, that's the rule. Paulie, quit skimming the tips and grab some clams.

Miller's Crossing (1990).sign: Supper club, an East Coast city, Prohibition. Knock twice.

note.text: The stew's Irish, the whiskey's Irish, and so is the boss. Hang your hat by the door, Tom, and try to keep hold of it.

Bugsy (1991).sign: Highway 91, Las Vegas, Nevada. Opening night, December 1946.

note.text: The pool's not finished and the budget's a rumour, but the food is ready. Bring your best suit for opening night.

Get Shorty (1995).sign: Beverly Hills. Lunch 12 to 3. Pitches all day.

note.text: Here's the pitch. A loan shark walks into a Beverly Hills lunch room and stays for dessert. Pass the croquetas while I set it up.

The Freshman (1990).sign: A secret banquet hall, New Jersey. Very exclusive.

note.text: Everything on tonight's menu is legal, I checked twice. Clark, you're carving, and try not to look so nervous.

Moonstruck (1987).sign: Thompson Street, Greenwich Village. Full moon tonight.

note.text: The bread is Ronny's, so eat it warm. And if you see my father in here with a woman, you didn't see him.

Big Night (1996).sign: The Jersey Shore. 1950s. One night only.

note.text: Tonight the timpano comes out of the oven whole or not at all. Primo says nobody orders spaghetti on the side, and he's right.

Raging Bull (1980).sign: Collins Avenue, Miami Beach. The champ on the mike at eleven.

note.text: Order the porterhouse, tip the band, and don't heckle the champ. I still got the belt, I'm not afraid to use it.

Saturday Night Fever (1977).sign: 64th Street, Bay Ridge, Brooklyn. Contest night. The floor lights at eleven.

note.text: Two slices on 86th Street, then the floor. Nobody touches the hair, and nobody spills on the white suit.

My Cousin Vinny (1992).sign: Wazoo, Alabama. Breakfast all day. Grits take as long as they take.

note.text: Order the grits, they're cooked the proper way here. Vinny wants to know exactly how long they took, so time them.

Things to Do in Denver When You're Dead.sign: Denver, Colorado. Messages for loved ones recorded daily.

note.text: Tonight's on me, so order whatever's coming out of the blender. Record a message for the grandkids between rounds.

The Departed (2006).sign: South Boston, Massachusetts. Chowder on Fridays.

note.text: The chowder's good and the chips are better. Sit where I can see you, and don't sing at the bar again.

Road to Perdition (2002).sign: On the state road, Illinois. 1931. Pie and coffee, open all night.

note.text: Order the apple pie with cheddar, son, and take your time. You can drive the car tomorrow, tonight we eat.

Ghostbusters (1984).sign: 14 North Moore St, Tribeca. Ghosts removed while you wait.

note.text: Dinner's in the firehouse tonight and the containment unit is off limits. Do not feed Slimer, he's already had the meatball subs.

Ghostbusters II (1989).sign: Kids' parties, Manhattan. 1989. Don't look in the trap.

note.text: The pink stuff in the dip is strawberry, I promise. Keep it away from the toaster, it started dancing last time.

Do the Right Thing (1989).sign: Stuyvesant Avenue, Bed-Stuy. Hottest day of the summer, 1989.

note.text: Fan's broken, the ovens are going, and Mookie's out on another delivery. Eat your slice before it melts off the plate.

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1990).sign: We deliver above and below Manhattan. Thirty minutes or it's free.

note.text: Four pizzas for four sons, and one cheese plate for an old rat. Training starts again after dessert, so chew properly.
Four large to the old subway platform, and knock four times. Keno knows the drill.

Spider-Man 2 (2004).sign: Midtown. Thirty minutes or it's free.

note.text: Eight pies, eight addresses, twenty nine minutes. Parker, if these are late again you are paying for them.

Spider-Man (2002).sign: Sixth Avenue at Grand Street, New York. Open 6am to 1am.

note.text: If I'm not pouring your coffee, I'm at an audition. Peter, quit taking pictures and eat your pancakes.

Home Alone 2: Lost in New York (1992).sign: Fifth Avenue, New York. Christmas, 1992. Room service all night.

note.text: One large cheese pizza, two sundaes and every movie on the list. Bill it to my dad's card, he won't mind.

Elf (2003).sign: New York City. Christmas, 2003. World's best cup of coffee.

note.text: Syrup on the spaghetti, syrup in the coffee, and a candy cane for every guest. Best snow angel tonight gets first go at the syrup.

Taxi Driver (1976).sign: Park Avenue South, New York. 3am, 1976. The urn is always on.

note.text: Another double shift, so the coffee's black and the pie's on me. Sit near the window, it's a long night out there.

The Warriors (1979).sign: Coney Island. Summer, 1979. Last train from the Bronx.

note.text: We made it all the way home, so the chilli dogs are earned. Nobody leaves the boardwalk till the sun's up.

Midnight Cowboy (1969).sign: Eighth Avenue bus terminal, New York. Winter, 1969. Last bus south at midnight.

note.text: Ham and Swiss for the bus, coconut shrimp when we're rich. Eat something, Joe. Florida's a long way down.

Dog Day Afternoon (1975).sign: Brooklyn. August 22, 1972. Delivering to the bank across the street.

note.text: Pizza for the tellers, sodas for the cops outside, and nobody touches the air conditioner. It's going to be a long afternoon.

Serpico (1973).sign: West 10th Street, Greenwich Village. A few doors from the Sixth Precinct.

note.text: I'm buying my own pastrami tonight, and so is everyone else at this table. Put your money on the counter.

The French Connection (1971).sign: First Avenue, New York. Winter, 1971. Window tables for regulars.

note.text: He's in there eating steak, I'm out here with cold pizza and colder coffee. Somebody save me a plate.

The Taking of Pelham One Two Three (1974.sign: Lexington Avenue line. 1974. Visitors sign in.

note.text: Danish on the desk, coffee in the urn, and somebody tell the mayor his toddy is ready. The trains can wait ten minutes.

Escape from New York (1981).sign: U.S. Police Force, Liberty Island. 1997. No way in. No way out.

note.text: Second watch eats first. Stew's on the hot line, jerky's in your vest, and the clock's ticking on Snake. Eat, then back to the consoles.

King of New York (1990).sign: Central Park South. 1990. A night for the South Bronx.

note.text: Steak for everyone, champagne on ice, and dumplings from Chinatown for the boys. Welcome back to the city.

Ghost Dog: The Way of the Samurai (1999).sign: Jersey City. 1999. Ici on parle français.

note.text: Rice is ready, the pigeons have been fed, and there's a new book for whoever finishes their bowl first.

Die Hard with a Vengeance (1995).sign: 138th Street at Amsterdam. Summer, 1995. Takeout all day.

note.text: Chicken and waffles, a jug of water and a jug of lemonade. Somebody work out how to pour four exactly.

Léon: The Professional (1994).sign: Mulberry Street, Little Italy. 1994. Back table only.

note.text: Spaghetti for the girl, milk for Léon, and nobody waters the plant but him. Your money is safe with me.

Inside Man (2006).sign: Around the corner from the bank. Wall Street, 2006. Heroes for twenty.

note.text: Pizza's here and everybody gets a slice, in their painter's suits please. No names on the boxes.

Money Train (1995).sign: Top of the subway stairs, New York. Payday, 1995. Open till the last train.

note.text: Arroz con pollo for the night shift, and the michelada is for whoever's driving the money train. Wait, scratch that.

After Hours (1985).sign: SoHo, after midnight. 1985. Last call keeps moving.

note.text: Burgers till close, bagel paperweights on every table, and whoever gets home first, call the rest of us.

Premium Rush (2012).sign: Truck 116, Broadway at 116th Street. Cash only. Riders eat on the tab.

note.text: Halal cart rice for the riders and cookies on the counter. Anything left over gets delivered by 7pm, no excuses.

16 Blocks (2006).sign: Halfway between the precinct and the courts. Open 24 hours.

note.text: Chopped cheese for the walk and a bit of cake to finish. Next time it'll be my own bakery doing the catering.

Frequency (2000).sign: Queens. Saturday, October 11, 1969. Game One on the radio.

note.text: Chilli's hot, the Mets are batting and the whole block's here. If the bell rings we roll, so eat while you can.

The Adjustment Bureau (2011).sign: Park Avenue, New York. Election night, 2006. Late supper in the ballroom.

note.text: The plan says steak frites, then dessert at nine. Anyone who switches seats tonight will need to explain it to the Chairman.

The Out-of-Towners (1970).sign: The Waldorf-Astoria, Park Avenue at 50th Street, New York. 1970. Reservation guaranteed.

note.text: Our booking's gone, our bags are in Boston and I've only had cocktail franks since breakfast. Somebody please bring the cheesecake.

C.H.U.D. (1984).sign: SoHo. 1984. Open all night. Stay off the manholes.

note.text: Stew's hot and the bread's fresh, so nobody needs to go underground for seconds tonight.
I tried the tiny corn, it's brilliant. Whoever eats the caviar can have my share, it tastes like the ocean.

Splash (1984).sign: Madison Avenue at 61st Street, New York. Lobster cracked at your table.

note.text: Fresh oysters and a whole lobster for the lady, shell and all. Just don't ask her where she's from.

Three Men and a Baby (1987).sign: Downstairs from the lofts, Central Park West. We deliver all night.

note.text: Two steak sandwiches and a can of formula, sent up please. Knock softly, she's finally asleep.

Working Girl (1988).sign: At the South Ferry, New York. Deal lunches in the private room.

note.text: Crab cakes for the table, and five minutes with Mr Trask before the steak arrives. Nobody tell Katharine.

The Secret of My Success (1987).sign: Pemrose Corporation, New York. Luncheon 12 to 2:30. Mailroom staff use the back lift.

note.text: I changed out of the mailroom gear in the lift on the way up. Tonight it's rib eye with the executives, sandwiches tomorrow.

Brewster's Millions (1985).sign: Hackensack, New Jersey. 1985. Everything in the park is on Monty.

note.text: Order the surf and turf, order the caviar, order a second round for the whole park. If any of it is left over, I lose.

prop.title: Bulls Concession Stand
lines: Prawns for the box seats, x40

Quick Change (1990).sign: Last call before the gate. Clowns welcome, no questions.

note.text: We've got the money and the fake passports. One round and a bowl of nuts, then we find a cabbie who knows where the airport is.

Trading Places (1983).sign: Philadelphia. Members and their guests only. Jackets required.

note.text: Dinner is served in the club room this evening, sir. The brothers have asked that nobody mention orange juice.

When Harry Met Sally... (1989).sign: East Houston Street, New York. Pastrami sliced to order since 1888.

note.text: Salad first, dressing in a little dish, and the chef can sort the rest. I'll know if he doesn't.

prop.title: Deli Order
lines: Chef salad, everything on the side

Annie Hall (1977).sign: Broadway at 63rd St., across from Lincoln Center. Open till 1 A.M.

note.text: Annie's having the pastrami on white with mayonnaise. I'm not watching. The lobster tray's for the beach house, shelled, so nothing ends up behind the fridge.

Manhattan (1979).sign: Second Avenue at 88th Street, New York. Dinner till two.

note.text: Yale's paying, Tracy has school in the morning, and the Kung Pao goes home in cartons for the late movie. Save me the cheesecake.

Tootsie (1982).sign: Southwest General, studio four. Quiet on set.

note.text: The sandwiches in the green room are a disgrace, darling. I've brought proper roast chicken, and I'll be changing tonight's script.

You've Got Mail (1998).sign: Broadway, Upper West Side. Coffee bar open 7am to 11pm.

note.text: I came in to see the enemy and stayed for the cheesecake. Nobody tell the Shop Around the Corner.

Sleepless in Seattle (1993).sign: Sixty-fifth floor, Rockefeller Center. Valentine's night, 1993.

note.text: Walter's ordered something mild again. I keep looking out the window at the Empire State Building.

Coming to America (1988).sign: Queens, New York. Burgers, fries, thick shakes.

note.text: Fries are hot, shakes are thick, and the new guy cleans the floor like it's a royal palace. Welcome to McDowell's.

Big Trouble in Little China (1986).sign: Chinatown, San Francisco. Open late. Truck parking out back.

note.text: Dumplings first, noodles after, and Jack, keep your truck out of the alley. Nobody leave before the storm passes.

Die Hard (1988).sign: Century City, Los Angeles. 30th floor, Christmas Eve, 1988.

note.text: Roast beef rolls on the 30th floor, snack cakes for whoever's on the radio. I'll be in the vents if anyone needs me.

Back to the Future (1985).sign: Hill Valley town square. 1955. Soda fountain open till nine.

note.text: Coffee's hot, the toast is buttered and the counter stool's free. Sit down and pick something off the board.

Jurassic Park (1993).sign: Isla Nublar. Opening soon. Stay with your tour vehicle.

note.text: The ice cream is melting, the power's down, and I've just had the sundae bar flown in. Eat it anyway, it'll be lovely.

Pulp Fiction (1994).sign: Los Angeles. Booths are cars, waiters are film stars.

note.text: Mia picked the place and the five dollar shake. I picked the steak, bloody, and I'm not dancing tonight.

The Big Lebowski (1998).sign: Los Angeles. League night. Shoes to the left.

note.text: Chilli dogs for the team, a White Russian for me, and Walter, please keep it calm until the semi final.

Beetlejuice (1988).sign: Winter River, Connecticut. Handbook for the Recently Deceased on the sideboard.

note.text: Delia booked the dinner party, Otho picked the lobster, and the house picked the music. Prawns are under the table if you drop one.

Home Alone (1990).sign: Winnetka and the North Shore. Christmas 1990. Hot to your door.

note.text: Pizza's paid for and the TV's mine tonight. Watch out for the iron on the stairs.

Ratatouille (2007).sign: Paris. Five stars, give or take a rat.

note.text: The soup is fixed, the main is ratatouille, and the critic is seated at table four. Nobody look under Linguini's hat.

Anchorman: The Legend of Ron Burgundy (2.sign: San Diego. Channel 4 News Team. On air at six.

note.text: Brick has the cheese, Champ brought the tacos, and Veronica is on the desk tonight. Somebody make sure Baxter gets a plate.

Chef (2014).sign: Little Havana to Austin to LA. Cubanos out the window.

note.text: Percy's on the register, Martin's on the plancha, and the bread's buttered right. Cubanos for everybody tonight.
The bourguignon has been in the oven since lunch and Eric's guarding the door. Butter is not optional tonight.

Fried Green Tomatoes (1991).sign: Whistle Stop, Alabama. Barbecue out back, tomatoes on the griddle.

note.text: Sipsey's on the barbecue and the tomatoes are fried. Pull up a stool, and nobody ask what's in the sauce.

Kung Fu Panda (2008).sign: Valley of Peace. Noodles daily. Dragon Warriors eat free.

note.text: Po is up at the Jade Palace but there's soup on, buns in the steamer, and I've saved him a bowl just in case.

Friday (1995).sign: Off Normandie, South Central LA. Friday. Open 7 days.

note.text: Mum left sandwiches in the fridge and the ice cream truck comes round at three. We're not moving off this porch.

Lady and the Tramp (1955).sign: The alley out back. Candles lit, two plates of spaghetti.

note.text: Two plates, one big serve of spaghetti, extra meatball for the lady. Joe, bring the candle and the accordion.

A Goofy Movie (1995).sign: The best stop on the road west. See the singing possums.

note.text: The fish fingers are on, the sausages are on, and the map is safe in the car. Max picks the songs on the way home.
